missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.

For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).

The retro-reflective devices shall have the resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected.
The lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall have only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
The lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall not include any logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, and the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON, the front or rear position lamp shall fulfill the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions.

The single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, except that these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.

While specific instructions are absent, the lamp shall not intentionally vary its photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

When there is doubt, the requirement that no red light shall be emitted to the front and no white light shall be emitted to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

The lamps (devices) shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle, where applicable.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except that this condition shall not apply to the optional rear lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

The electrical connections for rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11, except that if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
While daytime running lamps are not switched ON, the rear position lamp shall have a mandatory closed-circuit tell-tale.
The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
In the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

If any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source fails, then the single lamp shall ensure that at least one of the following provisions applies: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
The lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) shall have all measurements made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
When reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps are operated for 1 minute and for 10 minutes, the luminous intensities shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensities for all other lamps (other than those mentioned in 1.2.1), measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred, shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensity distribution shall, depending on the light source technology and in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, where the luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

extra.text: When the approval mark is affixed to the ESA according to paragraph 5.2. of this Regulation (Model A or Model B), the dimension a of the approval mark shall be 6 mm min.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection and measurement of the affixed approval mark against Annex 1 Model A/B. Pass if dimension a ≥ 6 mm and the layout matches the model.

extra.text: The ESA shall be tested for conducted emissions.
extra.test_case: UN R10 Annex 10 conducted transient emission test on the supply lines (switching of position, stop and reversing functions); pass if pulse amplitudes stay within the specified limits

extra.text: The ESA shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
extra.test_case: UN R10 Annex 9 ESA immunity test at the specified field strength over the required frequency range with lamp functions active; pass if no degradation of lamp functions (no flicker, unintended switching or loss of light output) per the test plan failure criteria

extra.text: The ESA shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
extra.test_case: UN R10 Annex 10 conducted transient immunity test on the supply lines with lamp functions active; pass if the lamp functions meet the required functional status per the test plan

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 measurement, 75-400 MHz; pass if broadband emissions are below the 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m logarithmically increasing limit (Appendix 6).

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 narrowband measurement from 75 to 400 MHz; pass if the measured level is below a limit rising logarithmically from 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m (Appendix 7).

extra.text: For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the supply lines shall be +75 V.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on 12 V supply lines; pass if the positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +75 V.

extra.text: For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the supply lines shall be -100 V.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on 12 V supply lines; pass if the negative pulse amplitude does not exceed -100 V in magnitude.

extra.text: For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the supply lines shall be +150 V.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on 24 V supply lines; pass if the positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +150 V.

extra.text: For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the supply lines shall be -450 V.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on 24 V supply lines; pass if the negative pulse amplitude does not exceed -450 V in magnitude.

extra.text: When tested with the stripline method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 stripline test, 20 to 400 MHz; pass if 60 V/m is applied over more than 90 per cent of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the stripline method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 stripline test, 20 to 400 MHz; pass if at least 50 V/m is applied at every frequency of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the TEM cell method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 TEM cell test, 20 to 200 MHz; pass if 75 V/m is applied over more than 90 per cent of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the TEM cell method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 TEM cell test, 20 to 200 MHz; pass if at least 62,5 V/m is applied at every frequency of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the BCI method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 bulk current injection test, 20 to 400 MHz; pass if 60 mA is injected over more than 90 per cent of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the BCI method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 bulk current injection test, 20 to 400 MHz; pass if at least 50 mA is injected at every frequency of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the ALSE method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 absorber-lined shielded enclosure test, 80 to 2,000 MHz; pass if 30 V/m is applied over more than 90 per cent of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the ALSE method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE test, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz; pass if 10 V/m is applied over more than 90 per cent of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the ALSE method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE test, 80 to 2,000 MHz; pass if at least 25 V/m is applied at every frequency of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the ALSE method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 ALSE test, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz; pass if at least 8 V/m is applied at every frequency of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the reverberation chamber method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, LUF to 2,000 MHz; pass if 21 V/m is applied over more than 90 per cent of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the reverberation chamber method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz; pass if 7 V/m is applied over more than 90 per cent of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the reverberation chamber method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, LUF to 2,000 MHz; pass if at least 18 V/m is applied at every frequency of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: When tested with the reverberation chamber method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
extra.test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz; pass if at least 6 V/m is applied at every frequency of the band with no degradation of immunity related functions.

extra.text: The starting profile test shall be applied to the ESA if it could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor.
extra.test_case: Review of intended vehicle installations; if the lamp may be fitted to M1 vehicles with ICE and 12V/24V starter motor, verify the starting profile test was performed and passed.

extra.text: When the conformity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) taken from the series is being verified, the broadband electromagnetic disturbance levels measured shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.5.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.10.2.1.
extra.test_case: CoP sample from series: broadband emission measurement per Annex 7 method; pass if measured levels <= reference limits of 6.5.2.1 (and 7.10.2.1 if applicable) + 4 dB

extra.text: When the conformity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) taken from the series is being verified, the narrowband electromagnetic disturbance levels measured shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.6.2.1.
extra.test_case: CoP sample from series: narrowband emission measurement per Annex 8 method; pass if measured levels <= reference limits of 6.6.2.1 + 4 dB

extra.text: When the conformity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) taken from the series is being verified, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength, expressed in Volts/m, up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.18.2.1.
extra.test_case: CoP sample from series: radiated immunity test per Annex 9 at field strength up to 80 % of limits of 6.8.2.1 (and 7.18.2.1 if applicable); pass if no observable degradation of lamp functions (e.g. no flicker, loss or unintended activation)

extra.text: If the conformity of the rear combination lamp (component or STU) taken from the series is being verified, the component shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1.
extra.test_case: CoP sample from series: conducted transient immunity test per Annex 10 up to levels of 6.9.1 (and 7.19.1 if applicable); pass if no degradation of stop/position/reversing functions

extra.text: If the conformity of the rear combination lamp (component or STU) taken from the series is being verified, the component shall not exceed the conducted emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1.
extra.test_case: CoP sample from series: conducted transient emission test per Annex 10; pass if emissions do not exceed levels of 6.7.1 (and 7.17.1 if applicable)

extra.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA (LED light sources and electronics of the rear combination lamp), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), shall not exceed in the 30-75 MHz frequency band the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m, where F is the frequency in MHz.
extra.test_case: ESA broadband emission measurement per paragraph 6.5.2.1. / 7.10.2.1. (Annex 7 method), 120 kHz bandwidth, lamp functions energised, scan 30-75 MHz; pass if all measured values are at or below 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m

extra.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), shall not exceed in the 75-400 MHz frequency band the limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m, where F is the frequency in MHz.
extra.test_case: ESA broadband emission measurement per paragraph 6.5.2.1. / 7.10.2.1. (Annex 7 method), 120 kHz bandwidth, lamp functions energised, scan 75-400 MHz; pass if all measured values are at or below 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m

extra.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), shall not exceed in the 400-1,000 MHz frequency band the constant limit E = 63 dBµV/m.
extra.test_case: ESA broadband emission measurement per paragraph 6.5.2.1. / 7.10.2.1. (Annex 7 method), 120 kHz bandwidth, lamp functions energised, scan 400-1,000 MHz; pass if all measured values are at or below 63 dBµV/m

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dB microvolts/m, for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 ESA narrowband radiated emission test, 120 kHz bandwidth, 30-75 MHz; pass if measured values ≤ 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at each frequency F (MHz).

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dB microvolts/m, for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 ESA narrowband radiated emission test, 120 kHz bandwidth, 75-400 MHz; pass if measured values ≤ 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at each frequency F (MHz).

extra.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m, for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 ESA narrowband radiated emission test, 120 kHz bandwidth, 400-1,000 MHz; pass if measured values ≤ 53 dBµV/m throughout the band.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the broadband emission test.
extra.test_case: Annex 7 paragraph 2.1: confirm the lamp is operated in normal mode with the maximum-load function combination (rear position, stop and reversing LEDs ON at rated voltage) throughout the measurement; pass if the operating state is documented and kept for the whole scan.

extra.text: The broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
extra.test_case: Annex 7 paragraph 4.1: scan 30 to 1,000 MHz in ALSE or OATS; pass if the emissions remain below the paragraph 6.5. broadband limits over the whole range.

extra.text: During the narrowband radiated emission tests, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 test; operate the lamp in normal operation mode, preferably with all functions (rear position, stop, reversing) energised at maximum load; confirm and record the operating state in the test report.

extra.text: The narrowband radiated emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
extra.test_case: Annex 8 test in ALSE/OATS; scan 30 to 1,000 MHz; pass if the emissions stay below the para. 6.6.2.1 narrowband limits over the whole range.

extra.text: The narrowband radiated emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
extra.test_case: Annex 8 test; verify the receiver or analyser detector is set to average.

extra.text: The ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9: absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5, or reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
extra.test_case: Review test plan and reports: confirm that the selected ISO 11452 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz with no gaps; pass if full range covered and ESA meets immunity requirements in each method.

extra.text: The frequency range and general test conditions for ESA immunity testing shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check test report references ISO 11452-1 for frequency range and general conditions; pass if conformant.

extra.text: The test conditions for the ESA immunity tests shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Audit test conditions (temperature, supply voltage, ground plane etc.) against ISO 11452-1; pass if all conditions conform.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
extra.test_case: During Annex 9 tests, energise rear position, stop and reversing functions in normal operating mode; pass if all functions are verified active throughout the test.

extra.text: All cables in the wiring harness of the ESA under test should be terminated as realistically as possible and preferably with real loads and actuators.
extra.test_case: Inspect harness terminations in test setup; pass if realistic/real loads used.

extra.text: The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check step size and dwell time in test report against ISO 11452-1; pass if conformant.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply when tested according to the method of Annex 10.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 conducted transient immunity test per ISO 7637-2 and ISO 16750-2; pass if lamp functions meet the immunity criteria of the Regulation.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply when tested according to the method of Annex 10.
extra.test_case: Annex 10 conducted transient emission measurement per ISO 7637-2; pass if emitted transients are within the limits specified.

extra.text: The rear combination lamp belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of drawings and sample: a marking area large enough for the approval marking and the markings of 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6. is provided.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: circle surrounding "E" and the distinguishing number of the approving country is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: four to six-digit sequential number matching the approval number is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: symbols for rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp per 3.2.4 are present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "148R" followed by the correct two-digit series of amendments is present.

extra.text: In the case of rear position lamps, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection with lamp in mounting orientation: arrow points outwards from the vehicle.

extra.text: If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "D" to the right of the relevant function symbol where applicable.

extra.text: If applicable, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "Y" to the right of the relevant function symbol where applicable.

extra.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
extra.test_case: If reduced light distribution applies, visual inspection: vertical downward arrow from a horizontal segment present.

extra.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: If external control gear exists, visual inspection: identification number and manufacturer name present.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Inspection on vehicle: single approval mark visible after installation.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
extra.test_case: Design inspection: no light-transmitting part can be removed without removing the approval mark.

extra.text: Each lamp submitted for approval (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp) shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
extra.test_case: Verify by review of the compliance matrix and test reports that each lamp function meets all general technical requirements of paragraph 4. and all photometric/colorimetric and other requirements of paragraph 5. of UN R148; pass if every applicable provision is met.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector of the rear combination lamp.
extra.test_case: Review against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes (series in force at application date); pass if each applicable provision verifiable at lamp level is met.

extra.text: The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 pertinent to each lamp function and to vehicle category M1, on which the lamp is intended to be installed, shall be applied where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Compile a per-function checklist of UN R48 provisions for M1 verifiable at lamp level (e.g. geometric visibility angles, colour, number, apparent surface); verify each on lamp samples in intended mounting orientation; pass if all are compliant.

extra.text: The lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps) shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which the lamps may be subjected in such use, the lamps retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
extra.test_case: After vibration/durability exposure representative of normal use, re-measure photometric intensities and colorimetric characteristics per UN R148 procedures; values shall remain within the prescribed limits for each function.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp or stop lamp is type approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", this shall be applied only to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps (not to the reversing lamp).
extra.test_case: Review of the type approval documentation and markings: the "D" marking appears only on the rear position and/or stop lamp functions and never on the reversing lamp function.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp or stop lamp is type approved as an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", this shall be applied only to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps (not to the reversing lamp).
extra.test_case: Review of the type approval documentation and markings: the "Y" marking appears only on the rear position and/or stop lamp functions and never on the reversing lamp function.

extra.text: The stop lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the stop lamp's apparent surface, optical components and outer lens texture. Pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the reversing lamp's apparent surface, optical components and outer lens texture. Pass if no logo is present.

extra.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
extra.test_case: Review the circuit diagram and inspect the LED PCB wiring. Disconnect one LED of each group and confirm that the whole group stops emitting light. Where it does, treat the group as one light source in the failure assessment of 4.6.1.2.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in paragraph 6.10.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of each single light source (or group) in turn and measure on the Annex 3 grid: every point shall be at or above the minimum. With all sources lit, the maximum shall not be exceeded. Alternatively, verify that the failure output signal for the tell-tale is produced on each simulated failure.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the stop lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in paragraph 6.7.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of each single light source (or group) in turn and measure on the Annex 3 grid: every point shall be at or above the minimum. With all sources lit, the maximum shall not be exceeded. Alternatively, verify that the failure output signal for the tell-tale is produced on each simulated failure.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the reversing lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in paragraph 6.4.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of each single light source (or group) in turn and measure on the Annex 3 grid: every point shall be at or above the minimum. With all sources lit, the maximum shall not be exceeded. Alternatively, verify that the failure output signal for the tell-tale is produced on each simulated failure.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, in case of failure of the variable intensity control the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control (e.g. open or short the control input) and measure intensity per Annex 3. The lamp shall automatically meet the steady-intensity requirements of its category without exceeding them.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, in case of failure of the variable intensity control the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control (e.g. open or short the control input) and measure intensity per Annex 3. The lamp shall automatically meet the steady-intensity requirements of its category without exceeding them.

extra.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
extra.test_case: Physical fitting trial: attempt to insert the light source in all possible orientations; pass if it can only be fixed in the correct position.

extra.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed applying.
extra.test_case: Dimensional inspection of the holder against the relevant IEC 60061 holder data sheet; pass if all dimensions and characteristics conform.

extra.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the light source(s) holder shall conform to the holder data sheet of IEC Publication 60061 relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s).
extra.test_case: Dimensional inspection of the holder against the IEC 60061 holder data sheet for the LED substitute light source category; pass if conforming.

extra.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), the module is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
extra.test_case: Cross-fitting trial of every module in each other module position in the housing; pass if modules with different characteristics cannot be interchanged.

extra.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensities of the lamp shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
extra.test_case: Photometry with LEDs continuously lit (steady operation); pass if setup confirms continuous operation.

extra.text: In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate lamp with applicant-specified control gear and settings during tests; pass if operating conditions match applicant specification.

extra.text: In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Operate lamp at applicant-specified conditions during photometry; pass if conditions match specification.

extra.text: If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously to the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
extra.test_case: Measure rear position alone and rear position+stop together over ±5° V / ±10° H grid; pass if ratio ≥ 5:1 at every point.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement in the reference axis per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (a); pass if luminous intensity ≥ 4 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady) and used as a single lamp, the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 1.7∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement over the full distribution per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no value exceeds 17 cd (except where the 60 cd allowance applies).

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R1 (steady) and is a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 8.5∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no value exceeds 8.5 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement in the reference axis per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (a) at all intensity levels; pass if luminous intensity ≥ 4 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable) and used as a single lamp, the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 4.2∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b) at all intensity levels; pass if no value exceeds 42 cd.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2 (variable) and is a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 2.1∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if no value exceeds 21 cd.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall meet the standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) defined in Figure A3-I and Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at the grid points of Figure A3-I per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (c); pass if each point meets the percentage of minimum intensity given in Table A2-1.

extra.text: If the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement below 5° down; pass if luminous intensity in that zone ≤ 60 cd and elsewhere ≤ the Table 4 maximum.

extra.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)), the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp shall be not less than 5∙10^-2 cd.
extra.test_case: Measure luminous intensity throughout the angles of geometric visibility per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if every value ≥ 0.05 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity in the reference axis (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on reference axis per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (a); pass if intensity ≥ 60 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady) and used as a single lamp, the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if maximum intensity ≤ 260 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady) and is a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 1.30∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if maximum intensity ≤ 130 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady), the standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) shall be as defined in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure at the grid points of Annex 2 Table A2-1 per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (c); pass if each point meets the required percentage of the minimum intensity.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Figure A3-I (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) shall be 3∙10^-1 cd.
extra.test_case: Measure throughout the geometric visibility field of Annex 3 Figure A3-I per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (d); pass if intensity ≥ 0.3 cd everywhere.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity in the reference axis (Par. 4.8.3.1. (a)) shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement on reference axis per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (a); pass if intensity ≥ 60 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable) and used as a single lamp, the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 7.30∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if maximum intensity ≤ 730 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable) and is a lamp marked "D" (Par. 3.3.2.5.2.), the maximum luminous intensity (Par. 4.8.3.1. (b)) shall be 3.65∙10^2 cd.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (b); pass if maximum intensity ≤ 365 cd.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable), the standard light distribution (Par. 4.8.3.1. (c)) shall be as defined in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure at the grid points of Annex 2 Table A2-1 per paragraph 4.8.3.1 (c); pass if each point meets the required percentage of the minimum intensity.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Figure A3-I (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) shall be 3∙10^-1 cd (day).
extra.test_case: Measure in day mode throughout the geometric visibility field of Annex 3 Figure A3-I; pass if intensity ≥ 0.3 cd everywhere.

extra.text: If the stop lamp is of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Figure A3-I (Par. 4.8.3.1. (d)) shall be 7∙10^-2 cd (night).
extra.test_case: Measure in night mode throughout the geometric visibility field of Annex 3 Figure A3-I; pass if intensity ≥ 0.07 cd everywhere.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (category AR) supplied shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0∙10^1 cd as given in Table 10 (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (a)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples per paragraph 4.8.3.1 at the reference axis/standard light distribution points; pass if intensity ≥ 8.0∙10^1 cd

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the h-plane, as given in Table 10 (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric scan of both samples in and above the h-plane; pass if no value > 3.00∙10^2 cd

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 6.00∙10^2 cd below the h-plane, down to 5°D, as given in Table 10 (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric scan of both samples from h-plane down to 5°D; pass if no value > 6.00∙10^2 cd

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D, as given in Table 10 (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (b)).
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric scan of both samples below 5°D; pass if no value > 8.00∙10^3 cd

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall comply with the standard light distribution defined in Figure A3-V (paragraph 4.8.3.1. (c)).
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of both samples at the grid points of Figure A3-V (Annex 3); pass if each point meets the required percentage of the minimum intensity

extra.text: Where type approval of the reversing lamp is granted applying the pair-only condition, the reversing lamp shall only be installed on the vehicle in a pair.
extra.test_case: Check communication form paragraph 9.1.3 and vehicle installation; pass if two reversing lamps are fitted as a pair

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard; however, for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the reduced angles of 20° inboard and 80° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Table A2-1 (CAD/goniometric sight-line analysis of the installed lamp at its intended outboard rear mounting position and height). Pass: the apparent surface is unobstructed across 45° inboard to 80° outboard, or 20°/80° below the H-plane when mounted below 750 mm.

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal; however, for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, 15° above and 5° below may be used, and for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm, 5° above and 15° below may be used.
extra.test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Table A2-1 at the declared H-plane mounting height. Pass: the apparent surface is unobstructed across 15° up/15° down, or 15°/5° when the H-plane is below 750 mm, or 5°/15° when it is above 2,100 mm (optional lamp).

extra.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard; however, for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the reduced angles of 20° inboard and 45° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Table A2-1 of the installed lamp. Pass: the apparent surface is unobstructed across 45° inboard to 45° outboard, or 20°/45° below the H-plane when mounted below 750 mm.

extra.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal; however, for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, 15° above and 5° below may be used, and for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm, 5° above and 15° below may be used.
extra.test_case: Geometric visibility check per Annex 2 Table A2-1 at the declared H-plane mounting height. Pass: the apparent surface is unobstructed across 15° up/15° down, or 15°/5° when the H-plane is below 750 mm, or 5°/15° when it is above 2,100 mm (optional lamp).

extra.text: The angles of geometric visibility of Annex 2 shall be applied as shown for lamps mounted on the right side of the vehicle and mirrored (inboard/outboard) for the opposite-side lamp.
extra.test_case: Review the geometric visibility analysis of both handed units. Pass: the inboard and outboard angles are correctly assigned relative to the vehicle longitudinal axis for the right-side unit as drawn and for the mirrored left-side unit.

extra.text: Unless specified otherwise, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 3 grid relative to the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°). Check that each derived minimum value is rounded down to three significant digits. Pass if every measured intensity is at least the derived minimum.

extra.text: In the case where the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the manufacturer's declared mounting height. If it is ≤ 750 mm, measure the Figure A3-I points down to 5° below H only. Pass if the minima are met in the reduced field.

extra.text: In the case where the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check the manufacturer's declared mounting height. If it is ≤ 750 mm, measure the Figure A3-I points down to 5° below H only. Pass if the minima are met in the reduced field.

extra.text: Within the field of light distribution of the stop lamp schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric scan between the grid points of Figure A3-I. Pass if the intensity at every intermediate direction is at least the lowest surrounding grid minimum.

extra.text: Within the field of light distribution of the reversing lamp schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric scan between the grid points of Figure A3-V. Pass if the intensity at every intermediate direction is at least the lowest surrounding grid minimum.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8) given by the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement at the Figure A3-I points with the applicable table minimum applied. Pass if all points are ≥ the stated percentage of the required minimum.

extra.text: The stop lamp of category S1 or S2 shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Table 7) given by the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement at the Figure A3-I points with the Table 7 minimum applied. Pass if all points are ≥ the stated percentage of the required minimum.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall emit, at the measuring points expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference, at least the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement at the Figure A3-V points relative to the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°). Pass if every point is ≥ the cd value shown in Figure A3-V.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the lamp functions shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN R148; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed boundaries.

extra.text: From a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, the mass-produced rear combination lamp shall conform to the requirements of this Regulation, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations.
extra.test_case: Conformity of production check: dimensional/mechanical inspection of randomly sampled lamps against the approved type; pass if deviations do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

extra.text: When testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation on any lamp chosen at random, no measured value of the mass-produced lamp shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: CoP photometric test per paragraph 4.8. on randomly chosen lamps; pass if no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by the mass-produced lamp shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed colour boundaries.

extra.text: The approval marking arrangement of the rear combination lamp shall be made in accordance with paragraph 3.3. of this Regulation; the arrangements shown in Annex 7 are given merely as examples.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the marking on the lamp against paragraph 3.3. of UN R148, using the Annex 7 examples for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (Figure A7-III) as reference. Pass if every approved function and its symbol (e.g. R/R2, S/S2, AR, retro-reflector class), the E-mark, the approval number and the series of amendments are arranged in accordance with paragraph 3.3.

extra.text: If the rear combination lamp contains light source modules, each light source module shall bear an identification code consisting of 'MD' followed by the approval mark (E-number) and the approval number of the lamp with which it has been approved, as in the example 'MD E3 17325'.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of each light source module. Pass if the identification code is present in the format 'MD' + E-number + approval number, and the code matches the approval of the lamp.

extra.text: For the reversing lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.1 after 1 min of operation (may be calculated from the distribution after photometric stability using the HV ratio); all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: For the reversing lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.1 after 10 min of operation (may be calculated from the distribution after photometric stability using the HV ratio); all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: For the rear position lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2 after 1 min (may be calculated via HV ratio from 30 min or photometric stability distribution); all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: For the rear position lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2 after 30 min or after photometric stability; all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: For the stop lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2 after 1 min (may be calculated via HV ratio from 30 min or photometric stability distribution); all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: For the stop lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement per Annex 8 para 1.2.2 after 30 min or after photometric stability; all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the rear position lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, comply at 4 seconds after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate (Table A8-1).
extra.test_case: Measure or calculate (ratio at HV) the intensity distribution 4 s after switch ON; all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the stop lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, comply at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate (Table A8-1).
extra.test_case: Measure or calculate (ratio at HV) the intensity distribution 0.2 s after switch ON; all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the reversing lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, comply at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate (Table A8-1).
extra.test_case: Measure or calculate (ratio at HV) the intensity distribution 0.2 s after switch ON; all test points within min/max limits.

extra.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be as defined in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimensions and compare them with the value for "a" in Table 1. Pass if the value is met.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection of the marking for the circle, the letter "E" and the country number.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: a 4 to 6 digit sequential number matching the approval number is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: the class symbol (e.g. IA/IB) matching the approval is present.

extra.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection: "150R" followed by the correct two-digit series of amendments is present.

extra.text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Review the rotational symmetry against the manufacturer's prescribed angles. Where needed, visually confirm that a horizontal "TOP" is on the highest part of the illuminating surface.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the marking shall be visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle (M1). Pass if the marking is visible.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed, no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
extra.test_case: Design review and disassembly check. Pass if no light-transmitting part (outer lens, reversing window insert) can be removed without also removing the approval mark or UI.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall meet the requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in those sections of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, pertinent to the retro-reflecting device and to the vehicle category M1 on which it is intended to be installed, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Review the retro-reflector design and its intended mounting position against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and the referenced Annexes (e.g. position, geometric visibility, orientation, colour). Pass if every requirement that can be verified at device approval is met.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C) without distortion.
extra.test_case: Part 1 of Annex 6: 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C on all ten samples, then visual inspection for distortion; pass if no distortion.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
extra.test_case: Water 10 min normal and 10 min inverted position; motor fuels 5 min; oils 5 min; visual inspection, colorimetry and photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if 5.1.3.2. met.

extra.text: If necessary, the retro-reflector shall withstand the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6 and the abrasive-strength test of the rear face in Part 5 of Annex 6.
extra.test_case: Corrosion 24 h + 2 h interval + 24 h; rear face 1 min; visual inspection, colorimetry, photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if 5.1.3.2. met.

extra.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand the test for stability in time of the optical properties in Part 3 of Annex 4 and the resistance to weathering test in Part 6 of Annex 6.
extra.test_case: Part 3 of Annex 4 and Part 6 of Annex 6, followed by colorimetry and photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if 5.1.3.2. met.

extra.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
extra.test_case: Colorimetry per paragraph 4.2. (visual, trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt) after each test group; pass if red night-time colour limits are met.

extra.text: Where more than one or a range of axes of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements with reference to each axis of reference or to the extreme axes of reference of the range specified.
extra.test_case: Repeat photometric measurements per Part 1 of Annex 4 for each specified axis / extreme axes; pass if Table 3 minima met for each.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angle β1 = 0°, β2 = 0° shall be equal to or greater than 3.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 3 photometry, α = 20', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 300 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angle β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0° shall be equal to or greater than 2.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 3 photometry, α = 20', β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 200 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angle β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20° shall be equal to or greater than 1.00∙10^2 mcd∙lx-1.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 3 photometry, α = 20', β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°; pass if RI ≥ 100 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 1°30' and illumination angle β1 = 0°, β2 = 0° shall be equal to or greater than 5∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 3 photometry, α = 1°30', β1 = β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 5 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 1°30' and illumination angle β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0° shall be equal to or greater than 2.8∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 3 photometry, α = 1°30', β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; pass if RI ≥ 2.8 mcd/lx.

extra.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI value of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 1°30' and illumination angle β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20° shall be equal to or greater than 2.5∙10^0 mcd∙lx-1.
extra.test_case: Annex 4 Part 1 para 3 photometry, α = 1°30', β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°; pass if RI ≥ 2.5 mcd/lx.

extra.text: If the Class IA or IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check declared mounting height; if < 750 mm, photometry downward angles limited to 5°.

extra.text: The mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be considered conforming from a mechanical and geometric standpoint only if the differences from the approved type do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of UN R150.
extra.test_case: Dimensional and visual inspection of random production samples against approved drawings; pass if deviations are within inevitable manufacturing tolerances and R150 requirements.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples per R150; pass if chromaticity coordinates lie within the prescribed colour boundaries.

extra.text: The mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall conform to the requirements of this Regulation from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations.
extra.test_case: Conformity of production check per Annex 3, paragraph 1.1: dimensional and mechanical inspection of randomly selected production samples against the approved type. Pass if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

extra.text: When testing the photometric performance of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Photometric measurement of randomly selected production retro-reflectors per Annex 3, paragraph 1.2, disregarding devices with apparent defects. Pass if every measured value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum value.

extra.text: The retro-reflective devices shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates.
extra.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of production samples per Annex 3, paragraph 1.3. Pass if the chromaticity coordinates lie within the boundaries prescribed for the retro-reflector colour.

extra.text: For testing the retro-reflection, the retro-reflector shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Verify light source calibration certificate for CIE Standard Illuminant A (2856 K) before photometry.

extra.text: During photometric measurements of the retro-reflector, stray reflections should be avoided by appropriate masking.
extra.test_case: Inspection of test set-up: masking applied around the retro-reflector and housing to avoid stray reflections.

extra.text: The background to the retro-reflector sample and the framework of the sample holder should be matt black.
extra.test_case: Inspection of test set-up: background and sample holder matt black.

extra.text: The light source and photometer head should remain stable throughout the period of the retro-reflector test, and the laboratory ambient temperature should not vary significantly during this period.
extra.test_case: Monitor source output, photometer reading and lab temperature during test; verify no significant drift.

extra.text: Sufficient time should be allowed for the photometric apparatus to stabilize before commencing measurements of the retro-reflector.
extra.test_case: Verify warm-up/stabilization period recorded before start of measurements.

extra.text: In the resistance to heat test for moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 1, paragraph 1: place the retro-reflector sample in a dry-atmosphere oven at 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 consecutive hours. Pass if the temperature and duration are logged within tolerance.

extra.text: If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
extra.test_case: Visual inspection after immersion; any clearly visible water on the reflecting surface = fail.

extra.text: The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min as measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform, the collector having a height of 100 mm and an inside diameter of a minimum of 140 mm.
extra.test_case: Annex 6 Part 3 para. 2.1.3: measure precipitation with the specified collector; pass if 2.5 to 4.1 mm/min.
